sections.h2: Which Union County offices touch a property tax bill?
sections.html:
Tax work stays in Morganfield, where the PVA and the sheriff share the 100 West Main Street address. The PVA describes itself as a state office with county jurisdiction, charged with valuing property as of January 1. Rates, the arithmetic and the collecting all belong to others.

  • PVA: PO Box 177, Morganfield, KY 42437. Call (270) 389-1933 between 8:00 and 4:00 on weekdays. Exemption forms go here.
  • Sheriff, the payee: PO Box 30, Morganfield, KY 42437. Phone (270) 389-1303, with the same weekday hours.
  • County Clerk, who records deeds and later holds unpaid bills: (270) 389-1334.

The county government site adds a tax roll search, a tax calculator and a rate page under the PVA menu, handy for checking a parcel before you call.

sections.h2: What sets Union County apart for someone selling a house?
sections.html:
Union occupies the state's northwest tip, looking over the Ohio River at the spot where the Wabash flows in. The county was created effective January 15, 1811, and together with Posey County, Indiana and Gallatin County, Illinois it marks the point where three states meet. Low wooded hills break up flat farmland, and the high point, 673 feet, is in the Chalybeate Hills inside the Higginson-Henry Wildlife Management Area. The county belongs to the Western Coal Fields region.

Four cities share the county: Morganfield, the seat and largest, plus Sturgis, Uniontown and Waverly. US 60, KY 56 and KY 109 carry the traffic, and the John T. Myers Locks and Dam, opened in 1977, stands 3.5 miles below Uniontown. Union County Public Schools runs elementary schools in Morganfield, Sturgis and Uniontown, one middle school and Union County High School, and the public library has branches in the same three towns.

Union has been losing people for decades. The 1900 census counted 21,326, and the 2020 count was 13,668. The July 2025 estimate is 12,839.

Employer businesses numbered 249 in 2023, with 3,980 jobs and payroll near $228 million, and employment grew 8.2 percent that year. Just over half of adults, 52.5 percent, hold or seek a job.

sections.h2: What does the state rate add up to on a Union County house?
sections.html:
Frankfort's real property rate for 2025 is 10.6 cents on each hundred dollars of assessed value, lower than the 10.9 cents charged in 2024. At the $104,500 median home value that is $110.77. County, school and other districts bring the full bill well above it.

The $49,100 homestead deduction brings the taxable base on that house to $55,400 and the state portion to about $58.72. Here, 21.9 percent of residents are 65 or older, and 23.1 percent of those younger than 65 live with a disability, so many households may be eligible. Apply at the PVA on West Main. A disability based claim needs yearly renewal. Veterans with service connected disabilities and owners deemed permanently and totally disabled by Social Security or Kentucky Retirement Systems do not have to renew.

sections.h2: What is the Union County payment calendar?
sections.html:
KRS 134.015 sets one schedule for all counties. Union's sheriff takes 2 percent off before November 2, bills the face amount until the year ends, charges 5 percent for January and 10 percent once February arrives, and tacks on a sheriff's fee.

On April 15 the sheriff gives the County Clerk its list of overdue bills and a lien goes on each parcel. According to the clerk's page, the sale of those bills normally falls in September, a year after the tax year, with the date put on the website roughly a month earlier. Anyone who wants to bid registers with the clerk first, and the state also requires registration for a buyer taking more than three certificates in this county, more than five statewide, or putting in more than $10,000.

sections.h2: What does a late Union County bill grow into?
sections.html:
The Department of Revenue shows the growth on a model $1,000 bill. A 10 percent penalty, the sheriff's add on and an assumed 4 percent commission lift it to $1,254.00 by the time the clerk receives it. Interest of 1 percent a month then runs, and commissions follow the interest.

  • With the attorney's first letter sent: $1,611.30.
  • If settled in May: $1,627.61.
  • Settled in June, after the newspaper notice: $1,659.90.
  • Bought at the sale by an investor: $1,704.21, not counting the investor's own charges.

Under KRS 134.420 the lien can last eleven years, and a new owner inherits it along with the land. If you owe back taxes, ask the clerk for a payoff number and let the title company send it at closing.

sections.h2: How does a Union County owner dispute an assessment?
sections.html:
Meet with the PVA before filing anything, since the state refuses appeals that skip that conversation. Each May the roll is displayed for thirteen days, beginning with the first Monday. After the meeting, hand the appeal to the clerk before the next day ends once display closes.

Local owners acting as the board of assessment appeals convene 25 to 35 days later, for as many as five days. It denies an appeal that lacks factual support, so collect sale comparisons, repair bids and photos. An owner who neither files nor shows up cannot go further to the Kentucky Claims Commission. Any change comes with a written reason, audio recording is allowed, and a higher final figure means an extra bill.

sections.h2: How are deeds and records handled by the Union County Clerk?
sections.html:
The clerk's office at 100 West Main Street holds recorded land documents going back to 1811, mostly deeds, mortgages, assignments and releases. A deed is lodged where the land lies and must cite how the seller got title (KRS 382.110). KRS 382.135 adds the parties' mailing addresses, the full price, an in care of address for that year's bill and a sworn price certificate.

The clerk offers e-filing so a title company can send documents without mail or courier. Residents searching for personal reasons can use the online index free, five searches a day, and the same books can be viewed in the office at no cost. Commercial researchers pay $65 a month per county through the records vendor.

An owner with a tenant, a probate delay or a house needing work can sell as is for cash instead of waiting for a retail buyer's inspection.

faqs.q: Where do I pay a Union County property tax bill?
faqs.a: Bring it to the sheriff at 100 West Main Street, Morganfield, or mail it to PO Box 30. Questions go to (270) 389-1303 during weekday hours, 8:00 to 4:00.

faqs.q: Does the Union County PVA send my bill?
faqs.a: No. The PVA only values property and handles exemptions, and the county's page says it leaves rates, tax calculation and collection to others. The sheriff handles billing and payment.

faqs.q: When is the Union County delinquent tax sale?
faqs.a: September, in the year after the tax year, is the usual month. The County Clerk posts the exact date on the county website about a month ahead, at (270) 389-1334 for questions.

faqs.q: Can I look up a Union County parcel online?
faqs.a: Yes. The county government site has a tax roll search and a tax calculator under the PVA pages, plus a rate page, so you can see the owner and assessed value.

faqs.q: How much is a house worth in Union County?
faqs.a: The Census midpoint for 2020 to 2024 is $104,500. That is well below the $172,000 in Trimble County and $258,000 in Warren County.
